criteria.text: A checked-in profile/coverage table traces every required #79 case to the approved Foundation contract and permitted standards/API sources. It distinguishes the applicable V4/R4 RC4 and AES-128 profiles, AES-256 R5/R6 input, R6 output, PDF-version constraints, and any source-grounded nonrepresentable combinations. Required successful cases are implemented; backend limitations are not converted into accepted unsupported results. Existing exclusions, including no new R5 output, remain intact.

Native `ALL_EXCEPT_METADATA` input and output work for every required profile, including AES-256. Public creation, reopening, and authorized protected rewrite return the declared scope, algorithm/revision, permissions, and credential authority. PDF 1.7’s qualified extension convention and PDF 2.0’s normative profile remain accurately distinguished.

Independent fixtures contain actual document-level XMP metadata and protected content. Observations prove the declared metadata bytes can be recovered without a document credential while protected strings, ordinary content streams, and other protected data require valid authentication. Document Info strings and other metadata-like values are not accidentally exempted. Merely observing `/EncryptMetadata false` is insufficient.

Actual original and emitted encryption dictionaries, crypt-filter selections, lengths/units, metadata-sensitive key derivation, credential authentication, and permission agreement match the frozen profile. AES-256 encrypted `Perms` agrees with `/P`, the metadata flag, reserved bytes, and required marker. Positive and single-defect negative controls demonstrate each required rule.

All-content AES-256 remains the secure default. Clear metadata requires explicit selection; obsolete output still requires request-scoped Legacy Security Mode. Missing, incorrect, destroyed, or invalid credentials and malformed/inconsistent scope declarations fail safely. Invalid preflight requests fail before caller work or publication, preserve existing destinations, and return declaration-ordered `NOT_ATTEMPTED` receipts.

Scope-specific behavior preserves independent owner proof, restricted-user permissions, existing credential preparation/boundary behavior, explicit owner-authorized protected rewrite, and named-Source anti-downgrade rules. Encrypted incremental publication preserves existing protection; it does not acquire an implicit scope-change path. Password authority continues to intersect with Existing Signature restrictions.

Native IN_PROCESS and HARDENED_WORKER execute the same applicable public contract successfully. Tests prove caller-owned streams/channels/credentials remain caller-owned, workflow-owned resources and temporary material are released on success and failure, outcomes are detached, and diagnostics expose no credentials, secret-derived values, content, paths, or backend exceptions. Publication failures retain the established receipt and destination guarantees.

The Migration Facade exposes the supported `DO_NOT_ENCRYPT_METADATA=8` selector and corresponding reader/writer behavior through real public calls, including combinations with admitted algorithms, copied properties, credential encoding, lifecycle, permissions, reopened files, and safe failures. Stable/Preview compiled surface and artifact contracts agree with the manifest; no unsupported Stable stub or #80 selector is added. Facade execution is recorded as its actual IN_PROCESS mode.

Separate mandatory syntax, standards, semantic, and visual chains pass for the new scope. Reuse the qualified infrastructure where applicable: qpdf syntax, independently qualified external standards checks, independent structural/content observations, and pinned PDFium/ImageMagick visual comparisons. Scope-specific models and controls preserve T78’s all-content checks. A tool’s exit status or producer label alone is not standards proof.

Acceptance recording and collection reject missing tools, uncovered required rules, undetected negative controls, invalid credentials, false execution modes, missing chains, changed/resealed findings, and mismatched identities. Retain exact original/randomized ciphertext hashes, raw safe findings, visual artifacts, configuration, source/contract/candidate identities, and producer/runtime hashes. Private credential files and temporary plaintext derivatives are cleaned up.

Certification covers exactly the actual Ubuntu 24.04 / Linux x86-64 environments for JDK 8, 11, 17, and 21: eight Native JDK/profile tuples, plus matching Facade IN_PROCESS behavior on every JDK. Evidence identifies the actual vendor/build, immutable image, Java executable, execution settings, and native/tool identities. Windows x86-64 and macOS x86-64/arm64 remain explicitly uncertified and nonblocking for Foundation 0.1.0.

The new child is compatible only after its evidence and dependencies pass. It retains parent `document.version-password-security`, Foundation dependency `password-baseline`, and inherited external gate `document.value.inspect-patch`; the incomplete aggregate is not made a prerequisite for independent child certification. `password-attachments`, aggregate `security`, and parent #33 remain incomplete.

Capability Matrix, Facade Surface Manifest, Foundation obligations/evidence, generated public views, authoritative English contracts/Javadoc, Chinese usage material, and `PROVENANCE.md` agree with the delivered behavior. New source/fixture/tool origins and licenses are recorded. Java 8 runtime/API compatibility, backend-neutral public signatures, and exclusion of acceptance-only tools/fonts/fixtures from product runtime remain verified.

The final candidate has fresh, valid same-candidate evidence for previously certified transactions, values, pages, metadata, annotations, text, images, incremental, and password-baseline obligations, followed by clear metadata. Historical records remain historical. Live readiness shows this member and its dependencies satisfied without regression of those retained obligations; unrelated Foundation blockers remain visible and may keep overall readiness NOT READY.

Include the actual new #79 tests whenever they live in separate suites, and exercise both Native profiles plus matching Facade behavior.

Ordinary Maven verification does not substitute for independent certification.
